detail.longDescription: I'm building a custom language that compiles to JavaScript. My compiler generates a plain JS string. Currently, I execute it like this: function DRL(){ dgsknlr = {}; fonksiyonlar = {}; var code = document.getElementById("kd1").value; var tokens = TKNRZ(code); var ast = PRS(tokens); var jskod = derle(ast.body); try{ var calistirfn = new Function( "dgsknlr", "fonksiyonlar", "ifadeHesapla", "matematikHesapla", "kosulDegerlendir", "cozArg", "hmbh", jskod ); calistirfn(dgsknlr, fonksiyonlar, ifadeHesapla, matematikHesapla, kosulDegerlendir, cozArg, hmbh); }catch (e){ console.error("Execution error:", e.message); } } The problem: new Function() runs in the global scope. Users can access window , document , and fetch , which is a security risk. Since I already have the compiled string, I don't want to rewrite everything as an AST interpreter. Question: What is the safest way to run this generated JS string in a browser sandbox, without eval or new Function , while still allowing me to pass specific variables (like a custom env object) into it? For context, the full source code of my interpreter is available on GitHub: https://github.com/turkum-webci/seairscriptv2.6
